title: Clustering: K-Means, Hierarchical and DBSCAN
description: How three unsupervised clustering algorithms - K-means, hierarchical and DBSCAN - detect natural groupings in unlabeled data.
content:
**Clustering** is a class of machine learning algorithms that solves the grouping of similar data points based on their features. It is an unsupervised learning methodology with the goal of detecting natural groupings within the input dataset.

**K-means** is a centroid-based algorithm that partitions data into K clusters.

How it works:
• It iteratively assigns data points to the nearest centroid.
• It updates each cluster centroid based on the mean of the data points within the cluster.
• The process continues until a certain number of iterations is reached.

Limitation:
• K-means is sensitive to the initial settings and results can vary depending on them.

**Hierarchical clustering** builds a tree-like hierarchy of clusters by recursively merging or splitting clusters based on their similarity. The result is a dendrogram - a tree-like representation of the dataset.

How it works:
• It starts by treating each data point as a separate cluster.
• It iteratively merges the closest clusters based on a chosen distance metric (e.g., Euclidean, Manhattan).
• The process continues until a certain number of clusters is reached.

**Density-Based Spatial Clustering of Applications with Noise (DBSCAN)** works by grouping together closely packed data points. It relies on two parameters:
• Epsilon - the neighbourhood radius around a point.
• Minimum number of points - how many nearby points are required to form a dense region.

DBSCAN defines three types of points:
• Core points - have the minimum number of points at distance epsilon from themselves.
• Border points - lie within epsilon distance of core points but do not have enough neighbours to be called core points.
• Noise points - points that are neither core nor border points.

How it works:
• It starts with randomly selecting a point and expands the cluster around it by recursively adding neighbouring points.
• The algorithm stops when all points are assigned to a cluster or labeled as a noise point.

**Quick comparison:**
• K-means - centroid-based; assigns points to the nearest centroid and updates centroids as cluster means; sensitive to initialization.
• Hierarchical - recursively merges or splits clusters by similarity; results in a dendrogram; uses distance metrics such as Euclidean or Manhattan.
• DBSCAN - density-based; groups closely packed points using epsilon and a minimum number of points; separates core, border and noise points.
